support_jen: FYI we have a customer on dedicated hosted inference hitting a bunch of 5xxs and connection resets since ~15:12 UTC. They pasted logs showing `tls: handshake timeout` and some DNS lookup failures. Raising here for triage.

ashok: Can you drop the customer's session id and example request? I want to correlate with edge logs.

support_jen: Customer session id: sess_8a3f. Example curl they ran: `curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` -> `curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`

support_jen: They also forwarded edge error snippet: `upstream response: tls: handshake timeout` and `resolver: lookup api.redwood-inference.com: i/o timeout`.

kevin: I'm seeing a small spike of resolver failures on our edge fleet starting 15:11-15:18 UTC in eu-west-1, same window. 5xx rate up ~6% for that minute for that shard.

sre_oncall: Any cert rotation activity around that time?

deploy-bot: certificate-sync job completed for cert-id cert-2026-03-15-15:10:23 on env=prod (job-id=certsync-8817) :white_check_mark: 

maria: Hmm cert-sync finished at 15:10. We have a known flaky path where certsync triggers a control-plane call that also blips our internal resolver cache eviction. Not supposed to, but I have a TODO.

ashok: Can we reproduce locally by forcing a resolver TTL flush + cert reapply? If yes this might be the same race.

kevin: I ran a quick repro on a staging edge: `dig +time=1 @127.0.0.1 api.redwood-inference.com` returned SERVFAIL intermittently after `systemctl restart cert-sync.service` — looks similar.

maria: Logs from the edge node during the window (sanitized):
```
2026-03-15T15:11:03Z edge-proxy[2451]: resolver: lookup api.redwood-inference.com: read udp 127.0.0.53:45123->1.1.1.1:53: i/o timeout
2026-03-15T15:11:04Z edge-proxy[2451]: tls: handshake timeout
2026-03-15T15:11:05Z edge-proxy[2451]: upstream connection reset; err="tls: server certificate mismatch"
```

support_jen: Customer reports intermittent 502/504 then CTL reconnects succeed after ~30s. They want SLA credit and explanation.

sre_oncall: Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) route traffic for that customer to alternative region pool, 2) temporarily pin to older cert version for that pool, 3) increase resolver retries on edge to reduce SERVFAIL impact. Which is quickest?

kevin: Easiest immediate is reroute to alt pool in us-east-1 (no config change on customer end). I can flip routing policy for that org id to the fallback pool. That will avoid the affected eu-west nodes.

maria: I'll schedule a hotfix to prevent cert-sync evicting resolver caches; patch ready in a PR but needs canary.

ashok: For the customer-facing reply: explain we saw transient DNS/resolver failures tied to a cert-sync job that coincided with certificate propagation. Apologize, provide timeline, and note mitigations. Also propose to proactively fail over their traffic as Kevin suggested.

customer-success-liz: I'll contact the customer with an explanation and offer to route them to a stable pool. Please confirm when the route flip happens.

kevin: Routing change applied at 15:40 UTC for org org_98765 -> fallback-pool-us-east. I verified successful requests from their sample trace after the change.

deploy-bot: rollback patch scheduled: roll-forward patch cert-sync-resolver-fix v0.1 canary at 15:56 UTC (canary group: 3% edge)

maria: Canary looks clean so far, no resolver evictions. If canary stays green I'll promote at 16:20.

support_jen: Customer notified, they confirmed traffic cleared and error rates dropped to baseline.

sre_oncall: Postmortem notes TODO: INF-1234 record: root cause - cert-sync job triggered resolver cache eviction under specific ordering leading to temporary DNS SERVFAIL and TLS handshake timeouts. Impact - transient 5xx/conn-resets for subset of hosted inference traffic in eu-west. Remediation - increase resolver retries, add lock in cert-sync to prevent eviction, monitoring alert for sudden resolver SERVFAIL spike.

ashok: Repro steps added to ticket INF-1234:
1) On an edge node, seed resolver cache for api.redwood-inference.com.
2) Trigger cert-sync (dev script: `./tools/cert-sync --id cert-2026-03-15`)
3) Simulate upstream DNS delay `sudo tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 200ms`
4) Run load of TLS connect attempts: `for i in {1..50}; do openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com < /dev/null; done`
Expect: intermittent handshake timeouts and lookup timeouts.

kevin: I've linked customer logs and edge traces to INF-1234 for SLA calculation.

customer-success-liz: Customer accepted the explanation and will wait for the postmortem. They asked for a credit; I'll open billing ticket referencing INF-1234.

maria: Follow-ups: schedule a permanent rollout of the cert-sync lock change, add unit test for resolver cache behavior, and update runbook for support to flip to fallback pool.

support_jen: Marking this thread resolved for now. Reopen if customer sees recurrence. :thumbsup:
